---
id: "smk-05"
title: "Peregrine falcon"
---

The peregrine falcon is a bird of prey found on every continent except Antarctica, making it one of the most widespread birds in the world. It has a blue-grey back, barred white underparts and a dark head with a distinctive moustache-like mark. The peregrine is famous for its hunting stoop, a high-speed dive in which it can exceed 300 kilometres per hour, the fastest speed recorded for any animal. It feeds almost entirely on other birds, which it strikes in mid-air. Peregrines nest on cliff ledges and, increasingly, on tall buildings and bridges in cities, where pigeons provide plentiful prey. Populations declined sharply in the mid-twentieth century because the pesticide DDT caused their eggshells to thin, but the species recovered after the chemical was banned and captive-bred birds were released. Peregrines have been used in falconry for more than a thousand years.
